A single day has room for the exercise and little else. The [companion curriculum](../../companion/index.qmd) takes each model and each argument of the day further, in modules that each stand on their own, so take the one that you need and leave the rest.

- [Panel data](../../companion/panel-data.qmd) takes the models of the day on the panel, output by output: the linear model, clustered errors, the two designs of fixed effects, standard errors with few clusters, and within and between.
- [Meta-analysis](../../companion/meta-analysis.qmd) puts the results of the five analysts on a common scale and combines them.
- [Causal graphs and adjustment sets](../../companion/dags.qmd) works through the graph of the day at a slower pace, and ends on a graph for a question of your own.
- [Weights](../../companion/weighting.qmd), [Missing answers](../../companion/missingness.qmd) and [The items behind the scales](../../companion/measurement.qmd) take apart the decisions about measurement that the menu opened.
- [The multiverse and its critics](../../companion/multiverse.qmd) sets out the debate in full, with its critics read against the curve of the claim.
- [Multilevel models](../../companion/multilevel.qmd) fits the claim at the level of the respondents, which the day leaves to the third day of the Extended course, and [Bayesian estimation](../../companion/bayesian.qmd) states the model of the claim as a posterior distribution.
- [Binary outcomes](../../companion/binary-outcomes.qmd) goes one step below the scales and fits a single item of the instrument as a yes-or-no outcome.
- [Building the analysis file](../../companion/data-management.qmd) shows how the panel was built from the survey files.
- [R on the country-year panel](../../companion/intro-r.qmd#sec-speccurve) ends on reading the specification curve of the case in R, aligned with the direction of the claim.
- [Reproducibility repositories](../../companion/repositories.qmd), then [Git and GitHub](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/git-github.html) on the AR4DS site, show how to archive and version the analysis that you declared.

The [AR4DS site](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/) describes the four cases of the course and holds its setup and help pages. The [Extended course](../eu-frames-extended/index.qmd) builds two more days around this workshop: a first day on open research and the tools, and a last day on the methods of the case and a report of your own, written in Quarto and kept under Git.
